query: What sample sizes are recommended for cognitive interviews and online pilots per country to ensure label comprehension and reliable pretesting?

response.query: What sample sizes are recommended for cognitive interviews and online pilots per country to ensure label comprehension and reliable pretesting?
response.answer: For cognitive interviews, a sample size of 15-20 participants is typically recommended. Online pilot studies usually require a minimum of 30 respondents per country to ensure reliable pretesting and label comprehension. These numbers help identify comprehension issues and improve survey design.

results.title: [PDF] GESIS Survey Guidelines - Cognitive Pretesting
results.content: 2.2 Cognitive pretesting Cognitive pretesting (or cognitive interviewing) belongs to the active pretesting methods because the participants' approach to answering the questions is actively probed and investigated (Beatty & Willis, 2007; Prüfer & Rexroth, 2005; Willis, 2005). Cognitive pretesting is usually conducted during the questionnaire design phase in order to obtain an insight into the cognitive processes that take place when questions are being answered: • How do participants interpret questions or terms? Cognitive pretests are particularly suitable for testing the comprehensibility of questions, identifying problems that respondents have answering the questionnaire, establishing the causes of these problems, and generating suggestions for improvement on the basis of these findings.
